case_name: Smt. Parul Tiwari vs Prashant Tiwari

parties.respondent_defendant: Prashant Tiwari and others (husband and family members)

facts_of_case: Petitioner's marriage was solemnised with respondent No.1 in 2009. Two daughters were born out of their wedlock. Respondents used to harass the petitioner for demand of dowry. Petitioner lodged a report at Mahila Police Station and FIR was registered against respondents.

legal_principles.principle: The power to quash criminal proceedings can be exercised when the parties have resolved the entire dispute amongst themselves.
legal_principles.held: Having overwhelmingly and predominantly the civil character, particularly those arising out of commercial transactions or arising out of matrimonial relationship or family disputes.
cited_cases: State of Madhya Pradesh Vs. Laxmi Narayan & others, (2019) 5 SCC 688
legal_principles.significance: HIGH — when parties resolve their dispute

legal_principles.principle: While exercising the power to quash criminal proceedings, the High Court must consider the antecedents of the accused and the conduct of the accused.
legal_principles.held: The High Court is required to consider the antecedents of the accused; the conduct of the accused, namely, whether the accused was absconding and why he was
cited_cases: State of Madhya Pradesh Vs. Laxmi Narayan & others, (2019) 5 SCC 688
legal_principles.significance: MEDIUM — to ensure fairness in quashment
